transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood CSM); Samir (Vertex CTO), Lena (Platform), Martin (Infra), Ava (Security), Diego (SRE)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) pilot. Main topics: network routing issues observed during throughput tests, transient KV cache warm-up behaviour, a small upgrade needed on the on-prem node image, and next steps for security docs and bench logs. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Networking / peering and egress rules
- Routing and NAT gateways (hairpinning issue)
- Model runtime upgrade (patch 1.3.4 -> 1.3.7) and compatibility
- Throughput tuning: batching, cache warm-up, sequence length distribution
- Security questions: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts

Transcript body:
00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we did a quick agenda - network status, perf numbers, upgrade plan, and security docs. Samir, want to kick off with a quick recap from your side?
00:12 Samir: Yeah thanks Jordan. Uh we've run the last two night runs, saw improved latency but some dropped connections when we hit the 1.5k concurrent session mark, and there is also this weird hairpin routing when calls originate from our private subnet to the on-prem endpoint and back through the NAT, so some replies got dropped.
00:29 Priya: mhm, that sounds like either the SGs or the NAT gateway is closing idle connections, or there could be asymmetric routing. Did you see any TCP resets in the SRE logs?
00:38 Diego: we saw a handful, mostly RST on the backend side. The packet capture shows SYN/ACK arriving but the ACK not making it back, so likely a path mismatch.
00:46 Priya: ok that maps to what we saw in our lab when hairpinning wasn't configured on the customer router. Jordan, I'll put the recommended route table entries in the diagram.
00:54 Jordan: great. Lena, you ran the throughput bench yesterday right? what were the numbers after the cache warm-up?
01:01 Lena: night run peaked at 1,600 qps but p95 latency was spiking around 620 ms for 512-token sequences until KV cache warmed. After warm-up p95 stabilized closer to 210 ms. So the main thing is warm-up behaviour; steady state looks good.
01:18 Priya: that's consistent with continuous batching plus KV cache. We saw similar where cold-starts pay a heavy tax - are you preloading prefixes in the workload?
01:26 Lena: not systematically. We have many unique session prefixes, so warm-up takes longer. Could you share the recommended prefix caching policy?
01:33 Priya: yes, we'll share a tuned policy. For high cardinality prefixes we usually recommend light-weight prefix caches and shorter TTLs, plus an initial synthetic warm-up run to prime the cache. We'll add a sample script.
01:47 Samir: also on the images - Martin found that the on-prem runtime we're running is 1.3.4 but Redwood's latest patch is 1.3.7 which includes a fix for the memory leak when doing long KV sessions. Is that required?
01:58 Jordan: the leak fix is important if you run long-running chat sessions. 1.3.7 also has a scheduler fix that improves batch packing for mixed seq lengths. We should plan a rolling upgrade.
02:10 Martin: any expected downtime? we prefer zero-downtime but can do a brief window if necessary.
02:15 Priya: rolling upgrades are designed to be seamless; nodes are drained and replaced. For our infra we've seen <5 minutes of capacity blips if your cluster is sized with 10% buffer. We'll provide exact steps.
02:24 Jordan: we'll propose a maintenance window for week of 2027-04-26, but we'll work with you to schedule.
02:30 Ava: security question - KMS integration: we attempted a test key rotation but couldn't complete the handshake. Is there a known incompatibility with our HSM provider?
02:39 Priya: not typically. Can you share the error text? sometimes the issue is the KMS IAM policy not allowing the Redwood service principal. Also make sure TLS hostname verification isn't failing if your HSM uses CNs that differ.
02:51 Ava: error log said "kms: unauthorized" and there was a mismatch in the key URI. I'll send the trace.
02:56 Priya: thanks, we can triage - Jordan will share the integration checklist for HSM/KMS.
03:03 Jordan: noted. Quick note on routing: in the last run we discovered the egress rules were too restrictive for our health-check probes, so some sessions were being marked unhealthy and traffic re-routed. If you allow ephemeral ports 1024-65535 for outbound to our control-plane IPs we won't get false failovers.
03:22 Martin: we were trying to lock down egress to reduce blast radius, but ok we'll open the ephemeral range to just the control plane.
03:29 Samir: on the perf front, we also saw a slight degen when sequences are uneven - many short docs and occasional long ones. Could batching unpacking be tuned?
03:38 Priya: yes, the runtime has batch packing thresholds. We'll send a config that prioritizes shorter sequences first (shortest-job-first packing) and caps batch size for long sequences. This reduces latency tail for mixed workloads.
03:50 Lena: that might help. Also, are there recommended quantization profiles to reduce memory use without losing quality?
03:57 Priya: for your use case we recommend 4-bit activations on the embeddings-heavy models and 8-bit for decoder-only variants; we'll provide the quant profiles we tested. Note quality regressions can occur, so do A/B tests.
04:10 Diego: one more networking oddity - during a spike we saw our 10gbe link saturate and packets dropped; Redwood's client retry logic then pushed even more work and exacerbated it. Any client backpressure config?
04:23 Priya: yes, we have client-side retry/backoff knobs. We'll recommend a backoff policy and a circuit-breaker threshold. Also auto-batching on the client can be tuned to avoid bursts.
04:34 Jordan: we'll include a recommended client retry/backoff doc and sample config.
04:39 Ethan: quick commercial note - we're tracking usage against the pilot committed units. We're a bit over on tokens this week due to test harness; Jordan I'll follow up on whether we can level set credits.
04:49 Jordan: yep I'll follow up with the finance side.
04:52 Samir: anything else on the security audit front? Ava?
04:55 Ava: yes, SOC2 and audit logs - we requested the SOC2 report and the long-retention audit logs. Do you have a sanitized copy for review and can Redwood support >1 year log retention for the on-prem audit trail?
05:07 Jordan: we can provide the SOC2 attestation and a sanitized report, and the platform can be configured to retain logs for >1 year in your S3-backed archive on-prem. We'll document the retention steps.
05:17 Ava: and RBAC - can we map Redwood roles to our SSO groups?
05:21 Priya: SAML mapping is supported; there are a few caveats around admin elevation flows. We'll share the SSO attribute mapping doc.
05:30 Samir: ok good. Back to the upgrade - Martin, do you have a preference for a canary vs. full rolling?
05:36 Martin: canary for sure, we'd like to observe memory patterns on the new image with 10% of traffic before ramp.
05:42 Priya: that's what we usually do - canary 10%, monitor for 24 hours, then incremental ramp to 50% and full. We'll provide the playbook.
05:52 Samir: timeline wise if we do the window week of 4/26 that's fine.
05:56 Jordan: action items recap: we'll send updated network diagram, upgrade playbook, batching configs, KMS checklist, and SOC2 docs. Samir/Team to run secure-bench and share logs.
06:07 Lena: small nit - when you say updated network diagram can you include CIDR ranges and exact SG lines? that speeds approvals.
06:13 Jordan: yes we'll include explicit CIDRs and security group rules and an example terraform snippet for peering.
06:20 Diego: on the bench logs, which verbosity level do you need? full pcap or aggregated metrics?
06:25 Priya: aggregated metrics plus a short pcap around the replicated failure window should be enough; full pcaps are heavy.
06:32 Martin: one more: when you provide tuned batching numbers can you include p50/p95/p99 and token costs? that's what the finance folks ask for.
06:40 Priya: yes we'll include p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost estimates for the pilot config.
06:46 Samir: ok thanks. Any blockers on our side?
06:50 Ava: I'll need the SOC2 and the KMS checklist to sign off. Without that security won't approve the upgrade window.
06:58 Jordan: understood, we'll prioritize SOC2 and KMS checklist.
07:02 Ethan: I'll schedule the upgrade meeting invite once we have the playbook and the proposed window.
07:06 Jordan: perfect. Quick check - competitors mentioned? any pushback we should be aware of?
07:10 Samir: a couple of infra folks pinged about Databricks managed endpoints and Anthropic for model quality but so far we're leaning to Redwood for flexibility.
07:19 Jordan: good to know. Last thing - Priya, can you drop the sample prefix-warm script and the batching config in the shared drive today?
07:25 Priya: yes I can get that by EOD.
07:28 Jordan: thanks everyone. We'll reconvene next week same time.
07:32 Samir: thanks, bye.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few swaps ("K-V cash" for KV cache, "SAM-el" for SAML), some speaker labels collapsed; manual notes added for clarity.
